title: Regional fallback quarantine and threshold realignment
creator: Nadia Chen
description: Summary: During a cross-region routing event on 2026-03-09 we observed a coordinated SLO miss (99th latency) across secondary regions when traffic was routed away from a degraded primary. The incident exposed a configuration gap between regional circuit-breaker hysteresis, autoscaler ramp settings, and KV-cache warmup behavior, which allowed a rapid fanout of hot prefixes into under-warmed secondary pools. This ticket documents the diagnosis, immediate mitigations performed, and tracked follow-ups to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2026-03-09 02:10 UTC - Regional monitoring alerted: EU-1 latency 99th > SLO threshold. 2026-03-09 02:12 UTC - Control plane triggered cross-region reroute per policy. 2026-03-09 02:13 UTC - Secondary regions began seeing request volume spike. 02:15 UTC - Queueing and token-generation latencies rose; oncall throttled global reroute. 02:25 UTC - Manual circuit-breaker adjustments and emergency capacity bump to dedicated pools. 03:40 UTC - KV-cache pre-warm tasks run for top-100 prefixes. 04:10 UTC - Latencies returned below SLO; rollout of gating changes started. 2026-03-09 05:00 UTC - Incident declared mitigated; follow-up investigation opened.
root_cause: Mismatch in cross-region routing policy and regional protective controls. The global reroute policy did not account for per-region cold-start characteristics: circuit-breaker thresholds in secondary regions used shorter hysteresis windows and lower concurrency limits; autoscalers were set with slow ramp-up (cooldown > 10m). The combination allowed immediate high-fanout traffic to overflow queues and expose cold KV caches, amplifying tail latency until manual intervention increased capacity and warmed caches.
contributing_factors: Circuit-breaker hysteresis configured differently across regions (EU/US/APAC drift)
Autoscaler ramp/cooldown too conservative for sudden cross-region failover
No pre-warm path for KV cache on large-scale reroute
Synthetic SLO checks did not simulate large fanout of identical prefixes
Global reroute policy lacked per-region admission gating (capacity-aware)
impact: ~1.5 hours of elevated 99th latency across EU and US secondary regions affecting 12% of production request volume; 4 enterprise customers reported increased error budgets and one escalated to SRE support. Billing-side retries increased downstream work for integrations.
immediate_remediations: Paused automated global reroute; applied temporary higher concurrency limit and extended hysteresis for affected secondary CBs; manually scaled up dedicated pools in EU-1 and US-2; triggered KV-cache pre-warm for top traffic prefixes; opened communication with on-call support for customer follow-up; created synthetic checks to validate warm caches post-fix.
long_term_action_items: A1: Normalize circuit-breaker hysteresis and threshold templates across regions and make region-specific overrides explicit (owner: Arjun Patel, estimate: 5)
A2: Implement capacity-aware gating in global reroute policy so automated failover respects downstream warm-up budget (owner: Priya Rao, estimate: 8)
A3: Add automated KV-cache pre-warm hook that runs prior to large-scale reroutes and on autoscaler scale-ups (owner: Miguel Alvarez, estimate: 8)
A4: Reduce autoscaler cooldown and add rapid ramp mode for emergency capacity (owner: Elisa Thompson, estimate: 5)
A5: Create a synthetic load test that simulates hot-prefix fanout and include it in canary pipelines (owner: SRE Team, estimate: 13)
A6: Update runbooks and run schedule: add explicit steps for circuit-breaker tuning and manual reroute pause/verify (owner: Nadia Chen, estimate: 3)
A7: Dashboard and alerting improvements: add per-region warm-cache metric and a derived 'fanout-risk' signal for reroute events (owner: Data Dogging Team, estimate: 5)
acceptance_criteria: Unified region CB templates checked into repo and covered by unit tests
Global reroute policy respects available warm-cache ratio and aborts if pre-warm fails
Synthetic fanout test included in canary with pass/fail gating
Runbook updated and SREs trained; at least one DR drill completed (scheduled)
